messages:
Maya Park: quick heads-up — ran the mixed-precision calibration sweep on model-rev4 today. found a weird tail effect when we used per-tensor int8 calibrators: a small fraction of sequences push latency way up with FP8 kernels enabled. attaching notes below.

Josh Kim: can you paste the perf excerpt? curious if it's kv-cache related or a kernel dispatch hot-path.

Maya Park: sure. here's the perf snippet from the failing run:

```
[2025-11-03 09:42:11] batch=64 seq=1024 active_kv=1 kernel=fp8-gemm median_tok_ms=0.78 p95_tok_ms=3.4 tail_tok_ms=9.8
[2025-11-03 09:42:11] batch=64 seq=1024 active_kv=1 kernel=int8-gemm median_tok_ms=0.85 p95_tok_ms=2.1 tail_tok_ms=2.3
[2025-11-03 09:42:12] batch=32 seq=2048 active_kv=1 kernel=fp8-gemm median_tok_ms=1.2 p95_tok_ms=6.7 tail_tok_ms=15.2  <-- outlier
```

Maya Park: that tail spike correlates with a couple long sequences in the calibration set. suspect per-tensor quantization is getting skewed by outliers and the runtime picks an fp8 kernel that doesn't handle these tails well.

Li Wei: interesting. did you try per-channel calibration? in our earlier tests per-channel stabilized activations and avoided those kernel fallbacks.

Maya Park: I did a quick rerun with per-channel calibrator + stratified sampling and the tail went away:

```
[2025-11-03 11:05:02] batch=32 seq=2048 active_kv=1 kernel=fp8-gemm median_tok_ms=1.15 p95_tok_ms=1.9 tail_tok_ms=2.2
```

Anita Gomez: what's the stratified sampling? how were you picking the calib examples?

Maya Park: proposal: split dataset by max-sequence-length bins (<=128, 129-512, 513-1024, >1024), then within each bin sample by token-frequency percentile (hot/mid/tail) so outliers don't dominate per-tensor statistics. also add a "sigmoid clipping" step on activation histograms to reduce extreme outlier influence before histogram merging.

Oz S.: sigmoid clipping? can you sketch the transform? sounds like another name for soft-clipping.

Maya Park: exactly — for each activation value x, we do x' = sign(x) * log(1 + alpha * |x|) / log(1 + alpha * M) * M where M is a chosen saturation point and alpha controls softness. keeps distribution shape but compresses extremes before building per-channel histograms.

Josh Kim: curious about impact on accuracy/regression vs perf. does that degrade logit-level quality for a few prompts?

Maya Park: ran eval on our holdout prompt set (2k prompts). WER/ROUGE changes were <0.3% relative with alpha=0.02, and perplexity shifted by +0.4 on avg. tradeoff seems reasonable given 2-4x tail reduction and FP8 kernel staying enabled.

Li Wei: two questions: 1) why does runtime choose fp8 kernel for these sequences? 2) could batching heuristics (batch size x seq length mix) be triggering a slow codepath?

Maya Park: (1) kernel selection policy currently prefers fp8 when model flagged as fp8-compatible and median activation range < threshold T. per-tensor outliers push median metric under threshold but create wide tails. (2) yes — the continuous-batching sampler sometimes groups a long sequence with many shorts, and the kv-cache warmup behaves oddly, creating extra memcpy/transpose calls. we've flagged a separate perf regression for that.

Anita Gomez: seems like two orthogonal mitigations: improve calibration dataset to avoid bad per-tensor stats, and make runtime kernel-selection more robust (e.g., check p95 activation width not just median).

Oz S.: +1. also consider a quick runtime guard: if we detect p95/median ratio > R for any layer during trace samples, fallback to int8 kernel or force per-channel quantization at serving time for that model version. cheap check and prevents spikes.

Josh Kim: FYI i ran a controlled microbench: same model, same batch/seq mix. enabling sigmoid clipping + stratified calib -> p95 token latency drops from 6.7ms to 2.1ms, and CPU overhead for clipping is negligible (0.5% of calib runtime).

Li Wei: nice. what about number of calibration samples? are we increasing dataset size? we should avoid exploding calib cost.

Maya Park: kept total samples ~5k, redistributed across bins. so no size increase, just stratification.

Anita Gomez: any changes needed in the calibration pipeline tooling? PR?

Maya Park: I'll open a draft PR: two changes — sampler stratification params + optional sigmoid_clip step (configurable with alpha/M). default off for now; we'll flip on for fp8 candidate models after a canary.

Oz S.: can we add a perf probe in the model-metadata that stores p95/median activation ratios per-layer so runtime can make an informed choice without re-running calibration?

Maya Park: yes, that's on my todo. will include a small JSON blob with per-layer stats in the build artifact. runtime can read it and apply the R threshold.

perf-bot: CI perf test queued: calib-sampler/stratified/alpha-0.02 — expected run time ~18m. will report back when finished. :robot_face:

Josh Kim: next steps: Maya to open PR, Li to add runtime guard RFC, Anita to schedule a canary on dedicated pool after PR merge.

Maya Park: filing PR now and will paste link here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
